description:
FILED s456ah (Opus agent AH, round 13), found by the #800 probe set.
PRE-EXISTING; EXPOSED (not caused) by #800's leaf-name fix.

perl's glob is bsd_glob, whose PATTERN language has a BACKSLASH ESCAPE: `\X`
is a literal X.  PCL's %p-glob-component-regex has no `\` arm at all -- it
escapes the backslash into the regex as a literal backslash -- so every
escaped spelling matches nothing.  Fixture: a directory holding gx*wild.dat,
gx?q.dat, gx[a]b.dat, gx\back.dat (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    pattern (perl source)   perl                 PCL
    glob("gx\\?q.dat")      gx?q.dat             (empty)
    glob("gx\\*wild.dat")   gx*wild.dat          (empty)
    glob("gx\\[a\\]b.dat")  gx[a]b.dat           (empty)
    glob("gx\\\\*")         gx\back.dat          (empty)
    glob("no\\?such.dat")   no?such.dat          (empty)

THE LAST ROW IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT, and it is why this is not a one-arm
fix: perl unescapes FIRST and then applies the #450 literal rule, so a
pattern whose every metacharacter is escaped is a LITERAL pattern and its
value is the UNESCAPED string -- returned whether or not the file exists.
So three sites move together, all in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:

  * %p-glob-component-regex  -- a `\X` arm emitting X as a regex literal;
  * %p-glob--wildcard-p      -- must SKIP escaped characters, or `no\?such`
                               takes the wildcard path and answers empty;
  * the literal arm of %p-glob--expand-one -- must return the UNESCAPED
                               string, not the raw pattern;
  and expand-glob-char-ranges runs before all of them and is itself
  escape-blind (`gx\[a\]b.dat` must not be read as a character class).

EXPOSURE NOTE (honest accounting): before #800 the ONE row that produced
anything, glob("gx\\\\*"), answered `gx\\back.dat` -- wrong, and wrong only
because the escaped LEAF (gx\\back.dat) happened to match the doubled
backslash the escape-blind regex demanded.  Two wrongs partially cancelled.
With #800's literal leaf the row answers empty.  Both answers diverge from
perl's `gx\back.dat`; what changed is the shape of the divergence, not its
presence.  Every other row was empty before and after.

NOT A #755/#800 REGRESSION: those two are the filename OUTPUT seam (a
matched leaf is rendered literally, by the one renderer %p-dirent-name).
This is the PATTERN side, which p-glob owns by design (DECIDED s455: "p-glob
is the one deliberate non-consumer" of %p-literal-path -- wildcard expansion
is its job).  It is that job that is incomplete.

BAR: the five probe rows above identical to perl; the dot-file rule, the
#450 no-metacharacter rule and the #488 brace note unchanged; a guard row in
Pl/t/wild-filename-01.t's oracle battery (it already builds a `s_\_n` file)
or in Pl/t/glob-01.t.
subject: glob PATTERN has no backslash escape: glob('gx\\?q.dat') answers nothing where perl answers the literal gx?q.dat -- and an all-escaped pattern is a LITERAL pattern (#450 rule) whose value is the UNESCAPED string
